model_scope: Isolated massive neutron star thermal evolution under magnetic-dipole spin-down, with a reduced initial-value model for core temperature, surface temperature, spin frequency, and central density. The model excludes binary recycling, companion ablation, detailed crustal heat blanketing, resolved neutrino microphysics, full equation-of-state integration, and non-spherical structure. Phase transition and superfluidity are represented through explicit scenario selection and effective coefficients.

parameter_requests.meaning: Gravitational mass of the isolated massive neutron star used to define the scenario and the EOS proxy domain.
required_conditions: Isolated massive neutron star; spherical symmetry; non-recycled spin-down history; no binary accretion torque.
retrieval_queries: measured gravitational masses of isolated massive neutron stars from pulsar timing and X-ray observations

parameter_requests.meaning: Initial core temperature at the start of the cooling integration.
required_conditions: Young isolated neutron star at the beginning of the cooling track; model assumes initial thermal state before long-term cooling; no crustal decoupling resolved.
retrieval_queries: birth core temperature estimates for young isolated neutron stars from X-ray observations

parameter_requests.meaning: Initial angular spin frequency of the neutron star.
required_conditions: Birth spin state of an isolated neutron star; magnetic dipole spin-down; no binary recycling or accretion-driven spin-up.
retrieval_queries: initial spin frequencies of isolated neutron stars from pulsar catalogs

parameter_requests.meaning: Initial central density used to seed the reduced density-evolution equation.
required_conditions: Adopted for the first executable parsimonious model; must be internally consistent with the selected mass and EOS proxy; no full EOS integration is resolved.

parameter_requests.meaning: Initial time derivative of the spin period, used with the braking index to evolve spin frequency.
required_conditions: Isolated pulsar timing measurement; magnetic dipole braking; no accretion torque; no significant magnetic field evolution resolved.
retrieval_queries: spin period derivatives of isolated massive pulsars from timing catalogs

parameter_requests.meaning: Critical density at which the adopted dense-matter phase transition is triggered.
required_conditions: Beta-equilibrated dense matter composition; EOS-dependent transition; relevant temperature and pressure regime for neutron star interiors.
retrieval_queries: critical densities for first-order phase transitions in dense matter equation of state databases

parameter_requests.meaning: Effective latent-heat release expressed as a core-temperature increment proxy for the reduced thermal model.
required_conditions: EOS-dependent phase transition; beta-equilibrated dense matter; conversion from microscopic latent heat to a temperature proxy is a model assumption; no resolved heat-capacity microphysics.
retrieval_queries: latent heats and specific heats for dense matter phase transitions in equation of state databases

parameter_requests.meaning: Explicit scenario switch selecting standard cooling, phase-transition cooling, or phase-transition cooling with superfluid modification.
required_conditions: First executable parsimonious model; scenario choice is explicit and not represented as a literature value.

parameter_requests.meaning: Index controlling the spin-down law used to evolve angular frequency from the initial period derivative.
required_conditions: Adopted spin-down law assumption; no resolved magnetic field evolution; no accretion torque.

parameter_requests.meaning: Effective timescale representing neutrino cooling and heat-capacity behavior in the reduced energy balance.
required_conditions: Parsimonious first executable model; detailed Urca processes, modified Urca processes, direct Urca thresholds, and superfluid pairing are not resolved separately.

parameter_requests.meaning: Effective coefficient relating core temperature to surface temperature in the reduced thermal model.
required_conditions: Spherical symmetry; simplified atmosphere boundary; no resolved radiative transfer or crustal thermal blanketing.

parameter_requests.meaning: Effective coefficient mapping spin-down angular acceleration to central-density change.
required_conditions: Small spin-down induced density changes; no full rotating EOS integration; moment of inertia response is absorbed into the proxy.

scientific_question: How does the surface temperature evolution differ between massive neutron stars undergoing spin-down induced core compression and those without, and can this distinguish the phase-transition mechanism from standard cooling?
symbolic_constraints: All physically meaningful temperatures, densities, masses, times, and coefficients must be positive.
The latent heat proxy must be non-negative.
The braking index must be non-negative.
The critical density must be positive and lie within the domain of the adopted EOS proxy.
The effective cooling timescale must be finite and positive.
The core-to-surface conversion coefficient must be positive.
The rotational compression coefficient must have a sign such that spin-down can increase central density.
Surface temperature is not an independent initial condition; it is derived from initial core temperature and the core-to-surface conversion coefficient.
Moment of inertia is not requested separately; it is absorbed into the rotational compression and spin-down proxies.
The phase transition is active only when the scenario selector denotes a phase-transition scenario and the central density exceeds the critical density.
Standard cooling disables latent heat release and superfluid modification.
The superfluid scenario modifies the effective cooling proxy only when the scenario selector denotes the superfluid phase-transition case.
The model assumes isolated neutron stars, spherical symmetry, and no binary recycling or companion-ablation evolution.
No detailed neutrino emissivity coefficients, thermal conductivities, or heat capacities are resolved separately in the first executable model.
symbolic_model_intent: Adopt a stiff ODE initial-value system in which core temperature evolves through an effective cooling proxy and optional latent-heat release, surface temperature is inferred from core temperature through an effective conversion coefficient, spin frequency evolves from an initial period derivative and a braking-index assumption, and central density evolves through an effective rotational-compression proxy. The phase transition is activated only when the scenario selector enables it and the central density exceeds the critical density. The superfluid scenario modifies the effective cooling proxy without introducing separate microphysical state variables. Moment of inertia and detailed EOS relations are not integrated independently; they are absorbed into the effective coefficients.
title: Thermal Signatures of Phase Transitions in Massive Neutron Stars: Distinguishing Spin-Down Induced Core Compression
